children.text: Fog of War — Starting position (White to move)

children.name: Caption
children.text: White sees only squares its pieces can move to: ranks 1–4. Ranks 5–8 and all of Black’s pieces are hidden in fog.

children.name: Real position label
children.text: Real position: every piece, no fog

children.name: Title
children.text: Fog of War: seven moves through White’s eyes

children.name: Intro
children.text: Each board is exactly what White sees after every move, White’s and Black’s. Fogged squares are ones no White piece could move to. When Black moves, White learns nothing unless something in view changes. Under each board, in blue, is where every piece really stood.

children.name: Move list
children.text: What actually happened:   1. e4 Nf6    2. Nc3 d6    3. Bb5 g6    4. Bxe8

runs.text: 1. e4 Nf6    2. Nc3 d6    3. Bb5 g6    4. Bxe8

children.name: Caption
children.text: White sees only the squares its pieces could move to: ranks 1–4. All of Black is hidden.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The pawn advance opens lines for the queen and bishop. White can now see out to a6, e5 and h5.

children.name: Caption
children.text:
Black moved, but nothing White can see has changed. White has no idea what was played.
Actually played: 1…Nf6, attacking the e4 pawn.

runs.text: Black moved, but nothing White can see has changed. White has no idea what was played.
Actually played: 1…Nf6, attacking the e4 pawn.

children.name: Caption
children.text: White can’t see any threat to e4, but defends it anyway. In the fog you guard against attacks you can’t see.

children.name: Caption
children.text:
Another invisible move. The board looks exactly the same.
Actually played: 2…d6, which quietly opens the diagonal from b5 to Black’s king.

runs.text: Another invisible move. The board looks exactly the same.
Actually played: 2…d6, which quietly opens the diagonal from b5 to Black’s king.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The bishop probes the a4–e8 diagonal and finds it open: Black’s king appears on e8. In normal chess this is check, but Fog of War gives no warning.

children.name: Caption
children.text:
Black moved again, and the king is still on e8. Whatever Black played, it didn’t deal with the bishop.
Actually played: 3…g6. No Black piece can move to b5, so Black never saw the bishop.

runs.text: Black moved again, and the king is still on e8. Whatever Black played, it didn’t deal with the bishop.
Actually played: 3…g6. No Black piece can move to b5, so Black never saw the bishop.

children.name: Caption
children.text: White captures the king and wins. Fog of War has no checkmate: taking the king ends the game.

children.name: Title
children.text: Fog of War: the real game, no fog

children.name: Intro
children.text: The same seven moves with the fog lifted, showing where every piece actually stood. The yellow squares mark the move just played, by either side.

children.name: Move list
children.text: 1. e4 Nf6    2. Nc3 d6    3. Bb5 g6    4. Bxe8

children.name: Caption
children.text: Both armies on their starting squares.

children.name: Caption
children.text: White’s king pawn takes the centre.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The knight attacks e4. None of White’s pieces can see f6, so White never learns of it.

children.name: Caption
children.text: White defends e4 without knowing it was attacked.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The d-pawn’s step clears d7 and opens the b5–e8 diagonal to Black’s king.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The bishop attacks the king on e8. In normal chess this would be check.

children.name: Caption
children.text: Black prepares …Bg7, unaware of the bishop on b5.

children.name: Caption
children.text: The king is captured and the game ends, with 15 Black pieces still on the board.
